title: On-call handoff draft - Priya Menon
content:
Context and purpose:
This is a personal, temporary on-call handoff + runbook draft I put together during the recent infra flakiness (INF-987). Not a polished canonical doc yet - mostly notes, quick commands, and a short mitigation play for whoever picks up the next shift.

SHIFT SUMMARY (2026-02-28 19:00 PST -> 2026-03-01 07:00 PST)
- Owner: Priya Menon (eng-sre) handing to next oncall: Noah Thompson
- Recent incidents: INF-987 (routing table thrash causing 503s to hosted-api), INC-2026-02-28-1 (degraded GPU node availability in us-west-2)
- State: Service returned to steady-state at ~2026-02-28 23:45 after temporary routing rollback. Dedicated capacity autoscaler disabled for affected pool pending root cause fix.

OPEN/ONGOING ITEMS (please check before leaving):
1) INF-987: temporary rollback applied to routing policy to use stable model-variant v1.4 across hosted-api. Root cause suspected: new kernel selection heuristic in the serving runtime (PR #342) interacting with pre-warmed cache eviction.
   - Current status: rollback active, monitoring for errors
   - Action items: monitor error rate, if <5/min for 1 hour, re-enable autoscaler in staging and run canary(s) before re-enabling in prod
2) Node availability in us-west-2: 2 GPU nodes marked unschedulable due to driver crash log pattern (nvidia-driver 525.60).
   - Current status: one node reprovisioned, one under investigation (ticket: INF-2026-02-28-NODE)

THINGS TO WATCH (first 30m):
- Hosted API 5xx rate (dash: /dash/hosted-api/errors) - threshold: >10/min triggers pager
- Queue depth on inference-redis (redis-infer-x) - if >1000, start temporary queue drain via rate-limit policy
- Autoscaler events for dedicated pool (dedicated-usw2-pool) - unexpected scale down is a bad sign

QUICK COMMANDS / PLAYBOOK EXCERPTS
- Check hosted API errors (prod):
  curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_TOKEN" https://api.redwood.ai/metrics/hosted/errors | jq .last_minute
- Restart affected agent (ssh to node):
  ssh ubuntu@gpu-03-usw2 && sudo systemctl restart redwood-agent && journalctl -u redwood-agent -n 200
- Disable autoscaler for pool (temporary):
  ./opsctl pool update dedicated-usw2-pool --autoscale false --reason "temp disable after INF-987"
- Rollback routing policy (if needed):
  ./opsctl router apply --policy stable-routing-v1.4 --env prod

TEMP MITIGATION NOTES (INF-987) - quick checklist:
- If 5xx spike observed and traces show KV cache misses + kernel fallback logs, do rollback to stable routing policy.
- After rollback: set alert for increased latency >200ms for 5m, to detect hidden tail latency regressions.
- Notify SRE Slack channel and tagging eng-serving-runtime and applied-ml.

TRIAGE NOTES / INVESTIGATION HINTS (for follow-up)
- Relevant PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/342 (kernel selection heuristic)
- Relevant logs: /var/log/redwood/serve-runtime/*.log and cloudwatch group /aws/rr/serve-runtime-prod
- Reproduction steps (staging): run long prompt workload (seq_len 2048) against canary pool with kernel-selection patched to instrument cache eviction counts.

COMMUNICATION TEMPLATE (to paste to Slack/Status page)
- Short status update: "We mitigated a routing-induced 503 spike by rolling back to stable policy v1.4 at 23:40 PST. Monitoring; traffic restored to normal. Root cause investigation in progress (INF-987)."
- Longer note for status page (if outage >30m): include timeline, impact, mitigation, and next steps

KNOWN WORKAROUNDS / TEMP PROCEDURES (to be converted to canonical runbook)
- If autoscaler triggers aggressive scale-down: immediately pin desired-replicas to current capacity and open ticket with release-engineering to investigate scaling policy flapping.
- If driver crash recurs on a node: reprovision node with driver 525.85 (known stable) and cordon old node: kubectl cordon <node> && kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data

Outstanding questions / TODOs:
- Who owns the final patch for kernel-selection heuristic? (assigned in PR #342 but needs eng-review)
- Add synthetic canary workload to catch KV cache eviction regressions (owner: applied-ml)
- Convert this doc into SRE canonical runbook under shared_drives/engineering/observability/oncall-playbooks (tracked: DOC-389)

HANDOFF NOTES TO @Noah:
- Primary: watch hosted-api errors + dedicated pool autoscaler.
- If you need escalation: ping Maya Singh (sr. SRE), Jordan Lee (serving-runtime), and Noah (platform-eng) - Slack thread linked above.

NOTES TO SELF:
- If I get a chance tomorrow morning, follow up with Ryan Patel about test coverage on kernel-selection and add an integration test that simulates KV cache churn.

END OF HANDOFF DRAFT

(quick rough doc - feel free to tidy and move to shared_drives. This is intentionally informal and assumes reader knows our opsctl and basic infra.)
